title: Transcendence degrees in scheme charts of a locally quasi-finite space map
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $Y$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $g:E\to Y$ be a morphism over $k$ which is locally quasi-finite, meaning that for every representable etale scheme chart $c:W\to E$, the scheme morphism $g\circ c:W\to Y$ is locally quasi-finite [def-weil-etale-morphism, pqf-def-quasifinite]. Write $|E|$ for its field-valued point classes with atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For every $e\in|E|$, every such chart $c:W\to E$, and every $w\in W$ mapping to $e$, one has $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(w)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(g(e)).$$ The fields and their $k$-structures are [def-weil-residue-field], and transcendence degree is [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Thus the left side is independent of the chart and its chosen point above $e$. No surjectivity of $c$, quasi-compactness, or separation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06RX (lemma-compare-tr-deg), specialized to E -> Y -> Spec k, evaluated in an arbitrary etale scheme chart; chart interpretation: definition-dimension-fibre and its following explanation.

proof.text: Fix $e$, a chart $c:W\to E$, and $w$ above $e$, and set $f=g\circ c$ and $y=f(w)=g(e)$. Give $W$ the $k$-structure induced by $c$. By the stated chartwise hypothesis, $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type] to see that $f$ is locally of finite type. In particular $f$ is quasi-finite at $w$. This uses this particular chart only; its surjectivity is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 06RX, lemma-compare-tr-deg, proof specialized to E -> Y -> Spec k; scheme-chart interpretation after definition-dimension-fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] to $f$ and $w$: its local finite type hypothesis was established in step 1. The corresponding point of $W_y$ is isolated. Now [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-residue-finite], with the same $f,w,y$, gives a finite residue-field extension $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(w)$. Its hypotheses are precisely local finite type and that isolated fibre point; neither global finite type nor finite fibres is required.

source.place: Tag 06RX, lemma-compare-tr-deg, proof specialized to E -> Y -> Spec k; scheme-chart interpretation after definition-dimension-fibre.

proof.text: The residue-field maps of [def-weil-residue-field] give a tower $k\to K\to L$, where $K=\kappa(y)$ and $L=\kappa(w)$, with the composite equal to the given $k$-structure on $L$: $g$ is over $k$, and taking stalk maps and then residue quotients preserves composition. The maps are injective by [def-pc-field-extension]. If $n=\dim_K L$, then for every $a\in L$ the $n+1$ vectors $1,a,\ldots,a^n$ are linearly dependent over $K$, producing a nonzero polynomial over $K$ that vanishes at $a$. Thus $L/K$ is algebraic. By both clauses of [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower], $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k L=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K+\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K+0=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K.$$ This is the desired equality; cardinal addition also covers infinite transcendence degrees.

source.place: Tag 06RX, lemma-compare-tr-deg, proof specialized to E -> Y -> Spec k; scheme-chart interpretation after definition-dimension-fibre.

proof.text: For two charts and points above the same $e$, apply the equality just proved to each. Both left-hand sides equal $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(g(e))$, so they equal each other. If a chart has no point above $e$ there is nothing to check. The argument made no quasi-compactness or separation assumption.

lean.statement: theorem trdeg_eq_of_chartwise_isLocallyQuasiFinite {k : Type u} [Field k] (Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] (E : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (g : E.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj Y) (hg : ∀ (W : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (c : yoneda.obj W ⟶ E.obj.obj), IsEtale c → (yoneda.preimage (c ≫ g)).left.IsLocallyQuasiFinite) (e : Point E.obj.obj) (W : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (c : yoneda.obj W ⟶ E.obj.obj) (hc : IsEtale c) (w : W.left) (hw : schemePointMap c w = e) : @Algebra.trdeg k (W.left.residueField w) _ _ (W.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap w).toAlgebra = @Algebra.trdeg k (Y.left.residueField ((yoneda.preimage (c ≫ g)).left w)) _ _ (Y.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap ((yoneda.preimage (c ≫ g)).left w)).toAlgebra ∧ ∀ (W' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (c' : yoneda.obj W' ⟶ E.obj.obj), IsEtale c' → ∀ w' : W'.left, schemePointMap c' w' = e → @Algebra.trdeg k (W.left.residueField w) _ _ (W.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap w).toAlgebra = @Algebra.trdeg k (W'.left.residueField w') _ _ (W'.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap w').toAlgebra
lean.note: Uses Over (Spec k) throughout, so g and charts are over k. The image g(e) is evaluated by the scheme composite represented by c ≫ g at w. The second conjunct states independence of the chart and the point above e; all residue-field k-algebras are the canonical ones induced by the structure morphisms.
